t: Hardware Tokens: Proof You Hold the Key
title: Hardware Tokens: Proof You Hold the Key
description: Hardware authentication tokens — YubiKey, PIV smart cards — prove identity with cryptography in tamper-resistant hardware instead of passwords in human memory. The private key never leaves the token; authentication is a signature challenge. Phishing fails because there is nothing to type and nothing to replay.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: FIDO2 and Passkeys
description: FIDO2 (WebAuthn + CTAP) is the open standard for phishing-resistant login: the token creates a per-site key pair, the site keeps the public key, and login is a signed challenge bound to the site's identity. Passkeys are the synced, user-friendly form. Defense systems require the hardware-bound form.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: PIV: The Federal Smart Card
description: PIV (Personal Identity Verification, NIST SP 800-73) is the US federal smart-card standard: the card holds certificates for authentication, signing, and encryption, unlocked by PIN. CAC cards are the DoD's PIV. YubiKeys can host PIV applets, bringing federal auth to a USB key.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: TOTP and HOTP One-Time Codes
description: TOTP (time-based) and HOTP (counter-based) generate one-time codes from a shared secret — the six digits in authenticator apps, also storable on hardware tokens. The server checks the code against its copy of the secret. Simple, offline-capable, and far better than passwords alone.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: OpenPGP on the Token
description: Hardware tokens store OpenPGP keys for signing and encrypting email and files — private key operations happen on the token, unlocked by PIN. Code and document signatures then carry hardware-backed identity. The YubiKey's OpenPGP applet is the common carrier.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: PINs, PUKs, and Lockout
description: Tokens protect keys with PINs and a PUK for unblocking: too many wrong PINs locks the token, and the PUK resets it — too many wrong PUKs destroys the keys. This is the anti-brute-force math that makes stolen tokens useless. Admins must record PUKs securely or accept the loss.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Touch-to-Authenticate
description: Many tokens require a physical touch to complete authentication — the human-presence test that stops remote malware from using the token silently. A signature will not happen without the finger. It is a tiny interaction with outsized security value.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

t: Attestation: Proving the Token Is Genuine
title: Attestation: Proving the Token Is Genuine
description: Tokens carry manufacturer attestation certificates proving they are genuine hardware — the same idea as the TPM EK. High-security enrollment checks attestation before trusting the token's keys. Counterfeit tokens get rejected at the door.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Deploying Tokens Across an Organization
description: Enterprise token deployment means provisioning (loading certs), PIN enrollment, help-desk flows for lost tokens, and revocation lists for departures. The logistics dwarf the cryptography. Successful programs treat tokens like badges: issued, tracked, revoked.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

t: PIV for Machine and Service Accounts
title: PIV for Machine and Service Accounts
description: PIV-style certificates also authenticate machines and services: servers prove identity with hardware-held keys, and code signing uses token-held keys. Humans are not the only identities. Every workload gets the same hardware-backed treatment.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Backup Tokens and Recovery
description: Every critical identity enrolls two tokens — primary and backup — because hardware gets lost and people go on leave. Recovery flows re-enroll without weakening assurance. One token is a single point of failure wearing a security costume.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Token Form Factors
description: Tokens come as USB-A, USB-C, Lightning, and NFC — the connector must match the fleet's devices, and NFC covers phones. Form-factor planning is unglamorous and decisive. The best token is the one people actually carry.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Standards Behind the Tokens
description: FIDO Alliance standards, NIST SP 800-63 (digital identity), and SP 800-73 (PIV) are the rulebooks tokens implement. Procurement cites the standards, not the brands. Standards are why tokens from different makers interoperate.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Revocation and Lifecycle
description: Certificates expire and get revoked; tokens get lost, reassigned, and retired. Lifecycle management — issuance to destruction — is the ongoing work after deployment day. A token program without lifecycle is a breach waiting for a calendar.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: The Token-Protected Organization
description: Ladder-top tokens: every human and workload with hardware-backed identity, phishing-resistant login everywhere, PIV for federal interop, lifecycle managed. Fifteen rungs from a USB key to an organization where stolen passwords are worthless.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.
